s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive lower limb weakness with fluctuating course and spinal involvement
salient_findings: Ascending spastic weakness of the lower limbs
key_facts: 18-year-old man
6 months of fluctuating lower-limb weakness
Initial episode of leg weakness resolved over 30 minutes
Asymptomatic for 4 months
Developed ascending spastic weakness over 3 months
Urinary retention requiring a Foley catheter
One month of constipation
No trauma, fever, steroid or other drug intake, or infections
Normal routine hematological and biochemical tests
Normal cerebrospinal fluid analysis
Unremarkable plain radiographs of the spine
Posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7 on MRI

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural lipomatosis
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7 on MRI, suggestive of fat

shortlist.label: Spinal cord compression
shortlist.why_kept: Progressive lower limb weakness with fluctuating course and spinal involvement

shortlist.label: Spinal epidural abscess
shortlist.why_kept: Urinary retention and constipation, possible signs of spinal cord compression or infection

shortlist.label: Spinal cord tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Ascending spastic weakness of the lower limbs, possible sign of spinal cord tumor

shortlist.label: Multiple sclerosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fluctuating course of lower limb weakness, possible sign of demyelinating disease

raw.rationale: The presence of a posterior epidural mass from D5 to D7 that is homogeneously hyperintense on both T1-weighted and T2-weighted MRI sequences, suggestive of fat, supports this diagnosis. The patient's symptoms of fluctuating lower-limb weakness, ascending spastic weakness, urinary retention, and constipation are consistent with spinal cord compression by the epidural mass.

rejected.label: Spinal cord compression
rejected.why: Too broad, as it is a symptom rather than a specific diagnosis

rejected.label: Spinal epidural abscess
rejected.why: Normal cerebrospinal fluid analysis and lack of fever or infection history make this unlikely

rejected.label: Spinal cord tumor
rejected.why: The MRI description of the mass as homogeneous and hyperintense on T1 and T2 sequences, suggestive of fat, does not support a tumor diagnosis

rejected.label: Multiple sclerosis
rejected.why: The presence of a specific epidural mass on MRI and the pattern of symptoms do not align with multiple sclerosis
